S5.01.note: The Chat tab bar shows no conversation title or brand text in the code read; the brand mark is only in the drawer.
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab (first screen).
Look at the top bar: menu button at the left, Chat/Work switch in the middle, temporary chat toggle at the right.
Tap the menu button to open the drawer and check the shell is still shown.
Compare with Expected: a persistent header with the primary actions for this view.
S5.01.where: Chat tab top bar on the first screen after sign-in: 'Open navigation drawer' button at the left, 'Chat or Work' switch in the middle, temporary chat toggle at the right

S5.02.needs: a signed-in account; Cloud needs an account with cloud unlocked
S5.02.note: Switching to Cloud is blocked when cloudUnlocked is false.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look at the switch under the search icon: it shows 'Local' and 'Cloud'.
Tap 'Cloud' (or 'Local') and watch the drawer list and the Chat screen change.
Compare with Expected: the user can switch between product areas or modes from the shell.
S5.02.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Local' / 'Cloud' switch at the top of the drawer; product areas are in the drawer list below

S5.04.needs: a Cloud account; a team workspace in the same account to see a second row
S5.04.note: Expected says the switcher is in the shell, but the drawer has no workspace control; the switch is on the Settings Workspace screen. The file useWorkspaceSwitcher.ts named in Code no longer exists; the switch calls switchWorkspace in apps/mobile/src/features/team/switchWorkspace.ts.
steps: Open the drawer with 'Open navigation drawer' and tap 'Settings'.
Tap the 'Workspace' row.
Look at the list: 'Personal' plus any team workspaces, and which one is active.
Tap another workspace row and check for the 'Workspace changed' alert, then compare with Expected.
S5.04.where: Settings > 'Workspace' > 'Personal' row and any team rows (not in the drawer)

S5.05.needs: phone width (on a wide window the sidebar is permanent)
S5.05.note: On the permanent tablet sidebar no collapse-to-rail control was found in the code read.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer' to open the sidebar.
Tap outside the drawer or swipe it closed to hide it.
Tap the button again to expand it.
Compare with Expected: the navigation hides and expands again.
S5.05.where: 'Open navigation drawer' button at the top left of the Chat tab (opens and closes the drawer)

S5.07.needs: a signed-in account with some chats
S5.07.note: The drawer has no inline search field; searching happens on the separate Search screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx).
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap the search icon at the top right of the drawer.
Type part of a chat title in the search field.
Compare with Expected: results filter to matching conversations.
S5.07.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Search' icon at the top right of the drawer (opens the Search screen, not an inline filter)

S5.08.note: 'New chat' is only in the drawer; no New chat button was found in the Chat tab top bar.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'New chat'.
Look at the Chat screen: a new empty chat should open.
S5.08.where: Open navigation drawer > 'New chat' (first row in the drawer list)

S5.09.note: In the code the Pinned section comes after the Projects section, not at the very top of the list.
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer and choose 'Pin'.
Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look for the 'Pinned' heading and the pinned chat under it.
Compare with Expected: pinned items sit in their own section.
S5.09.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Pinned' heading (appears after the Projects section, above 'Recents')

steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Find the 'Recents' heading.
Tap a conversation row under it.
Compare with Expected: the conversation opens.
S5.10.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Recents' heading and its chat rows

S5.11.needs: a project with chats in it
S5.11.note: The Projects section is on by default (FEATURES.projects is true in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts).
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Under 'Projects', tap the chevron beside a project that has chats.
Look for the chats listed under that project and the 'See all' link.
Compare with Expected: recent chats are shown grouped under their projects.
S5.11.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Projects' heading > project name > chevron 'Show chats in' the project

S5.12.note: The drawer itself does not group by date; grouping is on the chats list. The code heading is 'This Week' (capital W), and the date headings are literal English, not translated.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'See all chats' at the bottom of Recents.
Look at the date headings on the chats list.
Compare with Expected: Today, Yesterday, This week, Older.
S5.12.where: Open navigation drawer > 'See all chats' > the chats list with headings 'Pinned', 'Today', 'Yesterday', 'This Week', 'Older'

S5.13.needs: a signed-in account with at least two chats
S5.13.note: The row accessibility hint 'Long press for more actions' is a literal string in apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look at a conversation row: its title, a dot if unread, a pin icon if pinned.
Tap the active-looking row and note its highlight.
Tap another row and check that the chat opens and the highlight moves.
S5.13.where: Open navigation drawer > a chat title under 'Recents' or 'Pinned'

S5.14.note: No long-press actions were found on the drawer project row; project actions live on the project page (apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/settings/[id] route).
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap a project name under 'Projects'.
Look at the project page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the project opens.
S5.14.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Projects' heading > a project name

S5.15.needs: a Cloud account with AGI Work enabled
S5.15.note: The AGI Work row is in the folded More list and shows only when FEATURES.cloudTasks and showAgiWork are on.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'More' if needed, then tap 'AGI Work'.
Look at the task cards: each shows its state and origin.
Tap a card and check that the task opens.

S5.16.needs: a signed-in account with chats or projects
S5.16.note: Kind icons appear only while searching, and the icon in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx has no accessibility label in the code read. Drawer rows show no type icon, only a pin and an unread dot.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap the search icon, then type a word.
Look at the icon at the left of each result row.
Compare with Expected: each row shows its resource type.
S5.16.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Search' icon > type a word; result rows show a kind icon (chat, project, file, library, artifact, destination)

S5.17.needs: a Cloud account with a running task
S5.17.note: Drawer chat rows show no running marker in the code read; the marker is on AGI Work task cards only.
steps: Start a cloud task that is running.
Open the drawer, tap 'More' if needed, then 'AGI Work'.
Tap the 'Running' filter.
Compare with Expected: the running task is marked as running, and its card label includes the state.

S5.18.needs: a Cloud task waiting for approval or input
S5.18.note: The drawer chat rows have no needs-input marker in the code read.
steps: Open the drawer, tap 'More' if needed, then 'AGI Work'.
Tap the 'Needs you' filter.
Look for a card with a warning border and the line 'Waiting for your approval' or 'Waiting for connector input'.
Compare with Expected: blocked items are marked.
S5.18.where: Open navigation drawer > 'More' > 'AGI Work' > 'Needs you' filter

S5.19.needs: a chat with a new reply you have not opened
S5.19.note: The code read does not confirm that opening a chat clears the dot by itself; only the Mark as read action was confirmed.
steps: Open the drawer and find a row with a small dot (unread).
Long press the row and tap 'Mark as read'.
Look again: the dot should be gone.
Compare with Expected: unread marker clears when read.
S5.19.where: Open navigation drawer > a chat row with a dot; or 'See all chats' > 'Unread' filter

S5.20.needs: a signed-in account with chats; Archive and Share show only for Cloud chats
S5.20.note: Drawer rows have no visible overflow button; the ⋯ button exists only on the chats list. Share is shown only for non-temporary Cloud chats.
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer.
Read the actions: Rename, Pin, Move to project, Duplicate, Mark as read, Archive (Cloud), Delete.
Or open 'See all chats' and tap the row's 'More actions for' button.
Compare with Expected: share, rename, pin, archive, move and delete are present.
S5.20.where: Open navigation drawer > long press a chat row (actions sheet); or 'See all chats' > the row's 'More actions for' button

S5.21.needs: a signed-in account with a chat
S5.21.note: No Escape-key cancel was found in the code; the inline field cancels on blur, and Done saves.
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer.
Tap 'Rename'.
Type a new title and press the Done key on the keyboard.
Compare with Expected: the new title shows in the row and persists after reopening.
S5.21.where: Open navigation drawer > long press a chat row > 'Rename'; the title becomes an editable 'Chat title' field

S5.25.note: No forward navigation control was found in the code read; back is the only in-app history control.
steps: Open Settings, then open a sub-page such as Workspace.
Tap the back control at the top left (labelled 'Go back' on screens that set it) or swipe from the left edge on iPhone.
Look at the screen: it should return to the previous screen.
Look for a forward control: none was found in the code read.
S5.25.where: 'Go back' button on screens that have one (for example the Notifications screen); Android hardware back button

S5.28.note: On a phone the drawer menu button shows the unread count in its label but does not open notifications; the notification route is reached through search.
steps: Open the drawer and tap the search icon.
Type 'Notifications' and tap the result.
Look at the list: unread rows are marked 'Unread,' in their label.
Tap 'Mark as read' on a row, or 'Mark all as read', and check the unread state clears.
S5.28.where: Open navigation drawer > search icon > type 'Notifications' > the 'Notifications' result (phone); on tablet the 'Open notifications' pip button

S5.29.note: The drawer footer has no profile control; the entry is the Settings profile header.
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer', then tap 'Settings'.
Tap your profile header at the top of Settings.
Look at the 'Profile' screen: 'Chats' and 'Messages' counts and the AGI Cloud section with 'Subscription' and 'Log Out'.
Tap 'Log Out' and check the confirmation text, then dismiss it without confirming. Compare with Expected.
S5.29.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Settings' > the profile header at the top > 'Profile' screen

S5.30.note: No keyboard-shortcuts item and no separate support-contact item was found on the About screen; the 'Support' heading is the only group.
steps: Open the drawer, tap 'Settings', then 'About'.
Look at the 'Support' section.
Tap 'Report App Issue' to check that the feedback form opens, then go back.
Compare with Expected: help centre, support contact, feedback and shortcuts are in one place.
S5.30.where: Settings > 'About' > 'Support' section ('Help Center', 'Service Status', 'Report App Issue')

S5.31.needs: a Free account signed in on a build with native purchases, in Cloud mode
S5.31.note: Owner hold: FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, so Upgrade leads to the Subscription screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/cloud-billing.tsx), not a live purchase flow.
steps: Sign in to a Free Cloud account and switch the drawer to Cloud.
Open the drawer and look at the bottom: 'Upgrade' appears beside 'Settings'.
Tap 'Upgrade'.
Compare with Expected: the plan upgrade flow opens (currently the Subscription screen).
S5.31.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Upgrade' chip at the bottom of the drawer, next to 'Settings'

labels.text: You're offline. Local chats still work on this device.

S5.33.needs: a device or simulator whose network you can switch off
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi or mobile data on the device.
Look at the top of the screen for the banner.
Turn the network back on.
Compare with Expected: the banner clears when back online.
S5.33.where: Any screen after sign-in: turn off the device's Wi-Fi or network

S5.35.needs: a Free or paid account signed in; phone width (below the tablet split-view threshold)
S5.35.note: "Open navigation drawer" is an accessibility label, not visible text; the button shows only a menu icon. The code opens the drawer with a Back/Escape handler (src/features/shell/useDrawerDismiss.ts), but I did not confirm from code where focus lands after closing.
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen on a phone-width window (or an iPhone).
Tap the menu button at the top left of the header. It has no visible words; its accessibility label is "Open navigation drawer".
Check that navigation slides in from the left as a drawer over the content.
Press Escape on a keyboard, or tap the dimmed area beside the drawer, or use the Back gesture or key.
Check that the drawer closes and focus returns to the content behind it, as Expected says.
S5.35.where: Any main screen on a phone-width window (for example Chat) > tap the menu button at the top left of the header, labelled "Open navigation drawer" for screen readers

S5.37.needs: a tablet, or a window wide enough for the permanent sidebar
S5.37.note: This is a layout rule with no control of its own: src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts sets usesPersistentDrawer when the viewport is wide enough for the drawer width plus a minimum content width, and app/(app)/_layout.tsx uses drawerType 'permanent' when it is true. I did not read the exact width constants in this pass, and I did not confirm whether the menu button is hidden on the permanent sidebar.
steps: Open the app on an iPad, or resize the window to a wide size.
Sign in and look at the left edge of the Chat screen.
Check that the navigation list stays visible next to the content.
Make the window narrow again and check that navigation returns to a slide-in drawer.
S5.37.where: Tablet or wide window (iPad, or a resized window wide enough for the permanent sidebar) > the navigation sidebar stays on the left beside the content instead of a phone drawer

S5.38.needs: a paid or Cloud account; a temporary cloud chat; a second app to open the link from (for example Notes)
S5.38.note: Share link appears only for temporary cloud chats in the code I read. I did not find a stable link control for projects or tasks in apps/mobile, and the link route apps/mobile/app/(app)/open/[target]/[id].tsx redirects to home for an invalid target or id. The app scheme is agiworkforce and the https://agiworkforce.com/open/ prefix is declared in apps/mobile/app.config.js.
steps: Sign in with Cloud mode on, and open a temporary cloud chat.
Open the chat's action menu from the screen header.
Tap "Share link" and copy the link that appears.
Open that link on the phone, or in another app that opens links.
Check that the same chat opens directly in the app, as Expected says.
S5.38.where: Open a temporary cloud chat > its menu > "Share link"; then open the copied link on the phone (the https://agiworkforce.com/open/... address opens the app)

S5.39.needs: a second account, or a conversation or project that was deleted; for the missing page, a way to open an unknown address
S5.39.note: I did not confirm how a person types an unknown address into the app, so the missing-page step may need a tester-side link. The loading text "Loading Cloud project" is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/[id].tsx, and the chat loading state is a message skeleton in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.
steps: Sign in with an account that cannot see a chat or project (or use one that was deleted).
Open that chat or project from its link.
Look for the loading state first ("Loading Cloud project" or the message skeleton), then for the unavailable screen.
Check that the message on screen matches Expected: a clear unavailable message, not a blank screen.
For a missing page, open an address the app does not have and check that "Page Not Found" appears with a "Go Home" button.
S5.39.where: Open a chat or project that is gone or not in this account (for example from an old link) > "This chat is not available" or "Project unavailable" message; an address the app does not have > "Page Not Found" with "Go Home"
